encounters.summary: Presented with shortness of breath and bilateral lower-extremity edema. Chest imaging noted pulmonary vascular congestion.
Urine output improved after diuresis. Oxygen requirement decreased. Renal function remained stable.
Symptoms improved and the patient was discharged with follow-up instructions.
Admitted for evaluation of jaundice and abdominal distension. Ultrasound showed nodular liver morphology and ascites.
Diagnostic paracentesis was performed. Culture result was documented for clinician review.
Presented with fever, dysuria, and flank discomfort. Urinalysis was positive for leukocyte esterase and nitrites.
Fever resolved and oral intake improved. Discharge documentation recorded a completed inpatient antibiotic course.
